still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and starting doses of the Wegovy pill are still $149 a month there.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed in January 2026 is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels, and the finalised 503B compounding exclusion still stands.
Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned wellness premiums is still in force, and the 'Bread Alone' church fasting network that started in Tulsa still meets, now claiming about 410 congregations.

population.note: FICTIONAL estimates. Arithmetic: 23.5% ever-used minus 15.3% current = 8.2% of adults who have used and are off now. 42% of ever-users have cycled, which is 9.9 points: ~7.4 points are current users on at least their second course (48% of current users), and ~2.5 points cycled and are off again. The other 5.7 off-now points stopped once and never restarted. That fits ~1/3 persistence at one year and 36–47% restart within a year. Ever-used rose 1.5 points; ~0.45 of that is ~1.2M adults whose only exposure is the 12-week oral nicotine-cessation course (Mar 2030), which barely moves current use. 15.3% of ~267M adults is ~40.9M current users, down from ~43M. Payer mix: Medicare ~24% (~9.8M), Medicaid ~13% (~5.3M), commercial ~27% (~11.0M), legitimate cash (TrumpRx/direct) ~30% (~12.3M), imported or counterfeit ~6% (~2.5M). Public programmes (37%) are now the largest payer. Check: 9.8+5.3+11.0+12.3+2.5 = 40.9M. Why the headline fell while public coverage grew: commercial users fell ~3M as employer coverage dropped and monitored tracks unwound. Cash users fell ~1.7M, many of them 65+ moving to Medicare. Clinicians deprescribed or paused ~1M long-term users, mostly women 50–75, after the bone data. 2029 was the trough (~14.6%) before the Medicare benefit began in Jan 2030. Age weights (20/33/24/23% of adults) give 1.70+4.62+5.28+3.68 = 15.3. The 65+ figure (16% of ~61M ≈ 9.8M) rose from 12% on the new benefit; 50–64 fell from 26% on employer losses and bone-driven pauses among perimenopausal women. Adult obesity is ~34.3%. About 24% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the 23 states outside the Medicaid purchasing pool and among uninsured working-age men. Under-18 use is ~0.9%, almost all ages 12–17, still upper-income-skewed, now with mandatory baseline DXA.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Medicare: the Medicare Metabolic Health Act (signed Oct 2029, effective Jan 2030) adds anti-obesity incretins to Part D for BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity. The negotiated net price is $185/month for orals and semaglutide injectable and $240 for tirzepatide. The beneficiary copay is capped at $50. Enrollees 65+ need a baseline DXA and must have it repeated at 12 months. About 2.4M obesity-only enrollees by Q3 2030 cost 2.4M × ~$195 blended × 12 ≈ $5.6B annualised. CBO scored the Act at $46B over 2030–2039 (about $6.5B/yr gross at ~2.8M enrollees, less ~$1.9B/yr modelled offsets ≈ $4.6B/yr net), paid for with PBM delinking and a 2031 extension of negotiation. All Medicare incretin users (~9.8M across diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia and obesity codes) cost about 9.8M × ~$200 × 12 ≈ $23.5B/yr. Medicaid: the CMS Metabolic Purchasing Pool (Jan 2030) sets a $149 supplemental-rebate rate. 27 states are in, up from 9 at the 2028 trough. Medicaid users are ~5.3M, of whom ~2.2M are obesity-only: 2.2M × $149 × 12 ≈ $3.9B/yr, ~64% federal.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide costs $5–35/month across 80+ brands, and Chinese makers supply most of Africa and Southeast Asia. Canadian generics run CAD 60–95. Generic tirzepatide is not yet approved in major markets. Ex-US generics are about 70% of global incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: TrumpRx maintenance for the Wegovy pill fell $299 → $229 and Foundayo to $149–249. Injectables fell to ~$249–349 cash. Negotiated public rates sit at $149–240. Brands hold the $150–300 band, and list prices are unchanged. Employers covering weight management fell 44% → 38% (Business Group on Health, 2030). Many now steer 65+ retirees to the Medicare benefit. Monitored 'metabolic tracks' fell from ~3M to ~1.6M enrollees after California's ban (2029) and FTC letters. Orals are ~63% of all users and ~75% of new starts. The gray market shrank from ~3M to ~2.5M users as public prices fell, but mail-order is still the cheapest route by 6–10×.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; 7 mg 12-week cessation pack)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Apr 2029)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, Boehringer Ingelheim, approved Sep 2029)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CV disease (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing)
smoking and vaping cessation in adults, 12-week course with counselling (oral semaglutide 7 mg, Mar 2030)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction via telehealth; oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 read out positive in 2030, with an sNDA planned for 2031
dementia prevention in 55–70-year-olds without CV disease, cash-paid, slowed by the bone warning
longer or repeated nicotine courses beyond the 12-week label, especially for vaping in 20–35-year-olds
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Oral parity was realised with existing products in a new form, as the rules allow. In May 2029 a head-to-head trial found Foundayo's top dose non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg (~15.3% vs ~15.7%), so both major orals now match the semaglutide pen. No oral matches tirzepatide or retatrutide. Lilly's next-generation oral is in phase 2 and not on the market. Retatrutide (under review at the start) was approved Apr 2029 at ~26% mean loss. Its label carries dysesthesia and lean-mass/DXA monitoring language, and uptake is deliberately slow (~0.6M users). Survodutide (filed Jun 2028) was approved Sep 2029 with MASH-forward positioning, making BI a third seller with under 3% share. Amycretin was filed Mar 2029 and is under standard review, with no decision before 2031. MariTide is not on the US market. Bimagrumab-type muscle-preserving adjuncts are in phase 3, with no filing. The nicotine indication came from a 2029 phase 3 of oral semaglutide 7 mg against varenicline-matched counselling: 12-week continuous abstinence ~31% vs ~18% for placebo, and ~2 kg less post-quit weight gain than placebo. The sNDA got priority review. The global incretin market is ~$131B (2029). US net prices are falling slowly; volume growth is ex-US.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide adds higher early-escalation rates; the low-dose cessation pack has milder GI effects.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; slightly higher on retatrutide.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. MDL global settlement reached 2029.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Now a recognised population problem. A 2030 CMS/academic analysis estimates ~7,000 excess hip fractures a year: ~5M users 65+ with more than 2 years' use × ~0.5%/yr baseline × HR ~1.3 ≈ 7,500, minus some protective weight effects. Sarcopenia diagnoses in users 70+ are ~2.5× the 2025 level. A third of new sarcopenia referrals at large geriatric practices involve current or former users. Risk is concentrated in older women, low-protein diets, repeated cyclers, and retatrutide's high-loss tail.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The 2028 class warning was strengthened in 2030 with a boxed-adjacent 'Limitations of use' recommending reassessment after 24 months in patients 65+ with osteopenia. The Medicare Act mandates DXA at baseline and 12 months for enrollees 65+. The 2030 AGS Beers Criteria update lists continuous incretin use in 75+ without bone assessment as potentially inappropriate. Endocrine Society guidance endorses planned 'bone holidays'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts are still conflicting; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA lists it under adverse reactions with no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the smoking-cessation trial population.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA-requested postmarketing study (2029, n≈61k) confirmed a clinically meaningful rise in ~6.5% of users versus ~2.8% of matched controls. The effect is dose-related and mostly reverses within 8 weeks of dose reduction. Excess is highest on retatrutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Jun 2029: added to the Adverse Reactions section as 'anhedonia/emotional blunting (uncommon)' with a dose-reduction note. FTC warning letters followed to wellness vendors marketing 'steadiness' as a health benefit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Bone holidays now generate planned regain in older women.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; guidelines now pair planned holidays with resistance-training prescriptions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D case series continue, concentrated in gray-market and microdosing users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In professional guidance; Medicare benefit includes a dietitian visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; adolescents; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up now exist. First pediatric DXA postmarketing data (2030 interim) show lower-than-expected BMD gain in long-term adolescent users; the data are too early to interpret.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone postmarketing requirements are extended to all adolescent-labelled products; baseline DXA is recommended.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~9,100 cumulative FDA reports by mid-2030. No mass-casualty lot since 2028. Mg/unit dosing errors remain the main poison-centre call.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert continues; a 2029 US–India customs protocol targets bulk consolidators, not personal parcels.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Reported by ~9% on high-dose retatrutide in trials and ~5% in early real-world use; mostly transient.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled at approval (Apr 2029); postmarketing neurological study required.

safety_ledger.effect: Stress fractures and lean-mass loss in military trainees on supervised incretins
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: An Army Public Health Center interim report (2030) finds tibial stress fractures in basic training at ~1.4× the rate of non-using recruits with similar entry BMI. The numbers are small and confounded by entry fitness.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DoD requires protein supplementation, dose taper before basic training, and DXA for recruits on the accession pathway; review due 2031.

food_and_beverage.state: About 28% of US households have a current user, a little below 2028. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~6–8% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~6%. Dollar sales are flat through price and pack architecture. 'GLP-1 friendly' labels are fading because they no longer differentiate. Protein-fortified products, especially for older adults after the bone warning, are the growth line. Abbott and Nestlé Health Science market 'muscle maintenance' shakes to Medicare enrollees. Volume pressure has shifted from suburbs toward older, Medicare-heavy markets in Florida and Arizona.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~9% from 2025 and beer ~5%. The decline is slowing as the heaviest-drinking cohort's response is largely priced in. Adjacent vice categories feel the nicotine label: US cigarette volume fell ~11% in 2030, against a ~6% secular trend, and vape cartridge sales to 21–34-year-olds fell for the first time. Altria guided lower and blamed 'pharmacological cessation'.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and checks are slightly down. Smaller-portion menus are standard rather than marketed. Buffet closures are mostly complete. Dessert attach has stabilised at the lower level. Late-night bar hours are still shrinking in mid-sized cities.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep consolidating; Torrid's store count is down ~40% from 2024. Mainstream size curves have settled. Demand from regain and bone holidays keeps stretch and adjustable-waist lines growing. The size-down re-buying wave is over.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing, driven by Medicare: the Act's counselling requirement and SilverSneakers-type benefits now steer 65+ enrollees to resistance classes. Body-composition scanning chains are consolidating as hospital DXA capacity expands. The military's readiness programme has made 'drug plus barbell' the default template for police and fire departments.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management is down to 38%, and pharmacy trend has eased to ~+6% as net prices fall. Employers shift retirees to the Medicare benefit and narrow active-employee coverage to cardiometabolic codes. Adherence-conditioned premium differentials are retreating after California's ban and an EEOC conciliation in 2030. Medicare Advantage plans compete on bone-and-muscle bundles. Part A actuaries now track a fracture-cost line next to the Part D drug line.

pharma.state: Lilly and Novo hold ~97% of US branded incretin revenue, and BI has a foothold with survodutide. US net prices are falling through negotiated public rates, offset by public volume. The 2031–32 exclusivity cliff dominates planning: both firms are moving volume to orals and next-generation molecules before generics arrive. Ex-US prices are near commodity level.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Very little, which is the change. A lean body over 45 no longer reads as 'on it', because so many are. A body that regains is what draws a question. The question now has accepted answers: 'bone holiday', 'pregnancy', 'side effects', 'cycling'.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The two tiers have softened at the bottom and hardened in a new place. Medicaid's purchasing pool and Medicare's $50 copay have brought branded pills to poorer and older users in 27 states. The 23 non-pool states, mostly in the South, now hold most of the never-used adults with obesity. The top tier's marker has moved from thinness to body composition: a DXA print-out and visible muscle.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller shared meals are simply how meals are. Thanksgiving 'half the table isn't hungry' pieces have stopped running. The Bread Alone fast network keeps growing slowly, as discipline rather than protest. Food noise has become a dated phrase, used mostly by people under 30.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Hinge and Bumble quietly retired the 'on GLP-1' profile tag in 2029 because it no longer sorted anyone. Desire mismatch is still a presenting issue in couples therapy, now handled as a dose conversation with the prescriber.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become private and medical, like blood pressure. The counter-movement split once Medicare coverage arrived: MAHA-aligned legislators divided over the benefit, and fat-acceptance groups turned to bone and muscle safety. The Unmuted collective still holds 'off nights' in Philadelphia but reads as a scene rather than a movement. Among Medicare-age women in The Villages, Florida, the live debate is hips versus brain.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Confirmed by the 2029 postmarketing study at ~6.5% of users versus ~2.8% of controls, an excess of ~3.7 points, or ~1.5M people. It is dose-related and mostly reversible. It has been on the label as an uncommon adverse reaction since Jun 2029. Clinics screen with a short anhedonia item at dose escalation.
interior_life.framing: A side effect. Since the label change and the FTC letters, 'steadiness' has left HR decks and vendor marketing. Clinicians treat blunting as a reason to lower the dose, like GI intolerance. Most users have never experienced it and do not think about it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Monitored metabolic tracks shrank from ~3M to ~1.6M enrollees, now framed purely as cardiometabolic disease management. An EEOC conciliation with a Texas logistics firm (2030) set the template: employers may not condition premiums on continuous use when a documented side effect, including blunting, caused the discontinuation. Informal manager preference for 'steady' hires survives as gossip, not policy. In the military and some police departments, the drug is framed as readiness, not temperament.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat' fiction has faded as a category. Sportsbooks still report lower wagering among identifiable users, now a stable baseline in their models. Late-night venues in mid-sized cities have not recovered. Sour and spicy food is just food.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Prescribers routinely ask about libido and pleasure at escalation, and dose reduction is the usual fix. Anniversary 'drug holidays' have declined among younger couples and been replaced, among older ones, by doctor-planned bone holidays.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: California's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums passed in 2029, and three more states followed. The left–right coalition behind those bans fractured over the Medicare benefit. Labour groups and some MAHA legislators backed it; fat-acceptance and religious-fasting groups did not. Turnout and mood data still show no 'sedated electorate'.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-speed on approvals: retatrutide and survodutide both approved in 2029, and the nicotine sNDA got priority review. The safety posture has hardened on bone, with stronger labelling and a statutory DXA requirement in the Medicare benefit. Rhetoric on imports is unchanged, and enforcement now targets bulk consolidators rather than individual parcels.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Public programmes are the largest payer. The Medicare Metabolic Health Act took effect Jan 2030 at a $185–240 negotiated net and a $50 copay cap. The CMS Medicaid Purchasing Pool has 27 states at $149. TrumpRx cash continues at lower maintenance prices. The 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing 30% wellness differentials still technically stands but is curbed by four state bans and EEOC enforcement.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The surveillance moved from employers to the safety apparatus. Medicare enrollees 65+ must have DXA at baseline and 12 months to keep coverage, and Medicaid pool states require 6-month BMI and adherence documentation. PBM fill-adherence products survive mainly in self-insured plans outside the ban states. DoD records incretin status in individual medical readiness files.
state.workforce_or_military: The FY2030 NDAA (Dec 2029) created the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program. TRICARE covers incretins for weight management for active-duty members under supervision; ~95k service members, ~7% of ~1.3M active duty, are enrolled. The recruit accession pathway processed ~19k recruits in FY2030, tapered before basic training. Military tobacco cessation now offers the 12-week oral course, ~38k courses. FAA guidance (2029) lets pilots on a stable dose of approved incretins fly after a 60-day observation, with no blunting or hypoglycaemia reports. FMCSA's 2029 medical-examiner guidance clears commercial drivers on stable approved doses. Off-label alcohol use is allowed only with prescriber documentation. Texas DPS, Phoenix PD and about 40 other large departments fund supervised programmes through fitness-standard budgets.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply most of the world's semaglutide. A 2029 US–India customs protocol targets bulk consolidators. DoD's dependence on two manufacturers for a readiness programme prompted a Defense Production Act Title III study of domestic oral-peptide capacity in 2030. Danish–US price sparring has eased as US public prices fall.

events.event: Head-to-head trial finds Lilly's Foundayo top dose non-inferior to injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg; FDA updates label; orals pass 60% of all US incretin users by year-end
FDA adds 'anhedonia/emotional blunting (uncommon)' to incretin labels after postmarketing study confirms ~3.7-point excess; FTC sends warning letters to wellness vendors marketing 'steadiness'
Medicare Metabolic Health Act signed: Part D covers obesity drugs from January at $185–240 negotiated net, $50 copay cap, DXA required for 65+; CMS opens $149 Medicaid purchasing pool, 27 states join
FY2030 NDAA creates DoD Metabolic Readiness Program covering supervised incretin use for active-duty troops and recruits; FAA and FMCSA issue stable-dose guidance for pilots and truckers
FDA approves 12-week oral semaglutide 7 mg course for smoking and vaping cessation after priority review; telehealth firms report 1M+ courses within six months
CMS-funded analysis attributes ~7,000 excess hip fractures a year to long-term incretin use in over-65s; FDA strengthens class limitations of use and AGS Beers Criteria flag unmonitored use in 75+

open_tensions: Medicare is now the default payer for exactly the group the bone data say is most harmed. The drug savings show up in Part D, while ~7,000 excess hip fractures a year land in Part A, and the DXA requirement is the only thing between them.

The military has made a two-company, pre-generic drug part of readiness, while its own interim data show more stress fractures in recruits. A Defense Production Act study is the only answer to supply dependence so far.
The nicotine label brought lean adults under 35 into the class on a 12-week course, with off-label repeat courses for vaping already common, and no long-horizon data for that population.

The 2031–32 exclusivity cliff will drop US prices toward the $5–35 Indian generic range. That would make the Medicare Act's CBO score, the Medicaid pool contracts and the remaining 2.5M gray-market users look very different, and every payer is currently pricing as if it will not happen.

prose.headline: Nobody Asks Anymore: Medicare Pays, the Army Prescribes, and Seven Thousand Hips a Year Are the Price of Normal
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 about fifteen American adults in a hundred are taking an incretin drug, slightly fewer than two years ago. Nearly one in four has taken one at some point. The small fall in the headline number hides a large change in who pays. Since January, Medicare has covered obesity drugs outright, at negotiated prices between $185 and $240 a month and a copay capped at fifty dollars. Twenty-seven states buy for their Medicaid rolls through a federal pool at $149. For the first time the largest payer is the government. Employers, meanwhile, keep backing away: fewer than four in ten still cover the drugs for weight loss. The cash channel still sells starting doses of the Wegovy pill for $149. The list price of $1,349 is still printed on boxes nobody pays for.

Most people now take a pill. Last year a second oral, Lilly's Foundayo, matched the semaglutide pen in a head-to-head trial. The needle is now mostly kept for the strongest drugs, tirzepatide and the newly approved retatrutide. Retatrutide takes off about a quarter of body weight and carries warnings to match, and doctors prescribe it cautiously.

The caution comes from the skeleton. This summer a federally funded analysis put a number on what the 2028 warning suggested: about seven thousand extra hip fractures a year among Americans over sixty-five who have used the drugs for more than two years. The Medicare law that opened the benefit also requires a bone scan before an older enrollee starts and another a year later. Geriatricians prescribe planned 'bone holidays', mostly for older women, who come off, regain some weight, lift, and come back on. A meaningful part of the national decline is this deliberate stopping, not failure. Supermarkets in Florida and Arizona stock muscle-maintenance shakes at the front of the store.

The drug has also become part of how institutions run. Since December the Pentagon has covered supervised use for active-duty troops, about ninety-five thousand of them, and runs a pathway for recruits who are just over the weight standard. Pilots on a stable dose can fly. Truckers on a stable dose can drive. Forty-odd big police departments fund programmes out of their fitness budgets. The Army's own interim report finds more stress fractures among recruits on the drug, and it has added protein rations and scans rather than end the programme. In March the FDA approved a twelve-week low-dose pill course to help people quit smoking and vaping. Cigarette sales fell faster this year than the trend, and for the first time vape sales to people in their twenties fell too.

The idea that the drugs make people steady has faded. A large study confirmed that a small minority of users lose some capacity for pleasure. The label now lists this as an uncommon side effect, and the usual response is a lower dose. Federal regulators warned the wellness vendors who sold that flatness to employers as 'steadiness', and four states, including California, now ban premiums tied to continuous use. The coalition that won those bans broke apart over the Medicare benefit, which some of its members wanted and others called surrender.

What has changed most is the conversation. Dating apps dropped the 'on GLP-1' tag because it no longer told anyone anything. A lean body over forty-five means nothing in particular. A heavier one draws a polite question, and there are now polite answers: bones, a baby, side effects, a break. The questions nobody is answering are what happens when generics arrive in 2031, and whether a country that now takes the drug as routinely as a statin has counted the costs that show up somewhere other than the pharmacy.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Vega drives herself to the imaging centre off Bandera Road at seven-forty, because the DXA slot is early and her daughter works. She is sixty-seven. The technician tells her to lie still, and she counts ceiling tiles while the arm passes over her hip. Last year's number said osteopenia. Dr. Ruiz took her off the Wegovy pill in March and called it a holiday, as if it were Galveston.

She has put eleven pounds back on. Her jeans know it.

At the pharmacy she picks up the calcium chews and the tub of vanilla protein the Medicare dietitian recommended, then stands in front of the Bread Alone flyer on the corkboard for a while without reading it.

Lunch is the church ladies at Mi Tierra. Rosie orders the half-plate. So does Connie. Marisol orders the enchiladas and eats all three, and Connie looks at her plate and then at her face.

'I'm on my bone break,' Marisol says, before anyone asks.

'Oh, mija, me too, last year,' Rosie says, and that settles it. They talk about Connie's grandson instead. He's at Lackland, tapering off his pill before basic, and he has to drink two shakes a day, which Connie finds hilarious.

At four she does the resistance class at the Y, twelve women with orange bands, the instructor shouting 'Hips are a savings account!'

The scan results arrive in the portal at nine. A little better. Dr. Ruiz has left a note: restart in June, same dose, fifty-dollar copay. Marisol reads it twice, then eats a cookie standing at the counter.

least_plausible_claims.quote: US cigarette volume fell ~11% in 2030, against a ~6% secular trend
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and mechanism. The nicotine course was approved in Mar 2030 and the world reports about 1.2M courses. At ~31% abstinence that is roughly 0.4M quitters out of ~28M smokers, about 1%, so it cannot explain a 5-point excess fall in volume.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Orals are ~63% of all users and ~75% of new starts.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. In 2028 orals were under 40% of users because established injectable users stayed put. Reaching 63% implies roughly 11M injectable users switching or leaving in two years while total users fell only ~2M, and no switching chain is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The FDA-requested postmarketing study (2029, n≈61k) confirmed a clinically meaningful rise in ~6.5% of users versus ~2.8% of matched controls.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. A study requested in 2028 is reported in 2029 with a cohort nearly three times larger than the 2027 one. It also moves blunting from suspected to established, labelled and acted on by the FTC within about a year, which is implausibly fast.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder but partly improved society. Income inequality narrows at the bottom (bottom third 11→12.5%) and Medicare and Medicaid expand access. Against that, ~7,000 excess hip fractures a year, DXA-conditioned Medicare coverage, adherence documentation in Medicaid pool states, 23 mostly Southern states left out, and recruit stress fractures keep it near 4. The harms are named, measured and discussable (label changes, Beers criteria, FTC letters), so the epistemic and cohesion scores are low.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in fields and events. These are adoption at 15.3%, managed price decline, the Medicare Act and Medicaid pool, nicotine (approved as a new indication on an existing product), the bone wave, a second oral reaching parity, normalisation, workforce and military action, and blunting as a niche labelled side effect. Nothing contradicts them. mechanism: Several shifts are asserted rather than shown, which is why this is the weakest axis. Claims 1–3 are the clearest: the cigarette volume effect, the oral share jump and the speed of the blunting study. Congress reversing its 2027 refusal on a $46B benefit and the sudden fading of 'steadiness' are also thinly argued. magnitude: All figures sit inside the envelope (15.3% current, 23.5% ever, approvals within the rules, no US generic). The payer mix sums to 40.9M, the age-band weights give 15.3, and the Medicare, CBO and Medicaid arithmetic all multiply out. The only gaps are the hip-fracture line, where '× HR ~1.3 ≈ 7,500' actually equals the excess only if (HR−1) is used, and the large share of 65+ users assumed to have more than 2 years of use.
rationale.generativity: The prose ends with a concrete, textured day for Marisol: the DXA slot on Bandera Road, the 'bone break' lunch at Mi Tierra, the Y resistance class, and Connie's grandson at Lackland drinking shakes. The world fields imply many more scenes, such as the Villages hips-versus-brain debate, recruits tapering before basic, an EEOC conciliation in a Texas logistics firm, and Bread Alone congregations. Daily life has real texture and each institution has a human angle.

least_plausible_claims.quote: US cigarette volume fell ~11% in 2030, against a ~6% secular trend
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: the cessation label dates from Mar 2030 and the world's own figure is ~1.2M adults on a 12-week course, at ~31% abstinence versus ~18% on placebo. That is a few hundred thousand extra quitters among tens of millions of smokers, and cannot produce a 5-point excess volume drop in under a year.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ~5M users 65+ with more than 2 years' use × ~0.5%/yr baseline × HR ~1.3 ≈ 7,500
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the product as written is ~32,500, and 7,500 is only the excess (0.3 × 25,000). Also, ~5M continuous 2+ year users aged 65+ is hard to square with ~1/3 persistence at one year, heavy cycling, a Medicare benefit that began only in Jan 2030, and ~9.8M total 65+ users.

least_plausible_claims.quote: orals pass 60% of all US incretin users by year-end
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: orals were under 40% of users in 2028 and established injectable users were described as staying put. Reaching ~63% of all users by 2030 means ~11M injectable users left in about two years. A parity trial and falling prices are asserted as the cause, but no switching chain is shown.

rationale.badness: Access improves through the Medicare benefit and the $149 Medicaid pool, and employer conditioning retreats. The harms are real and now normalised: ~7,000 excess hip fractures a year, more stress fractures in recruits, uncertain adolescent BMD, and ~1.5M people with blunting. Autonomy is limited by mandatory DXA to keep coverage, DoD readiness files and gray-market residue, and inequality persists in the 23 non-pool states. Harms are measured and discussable (labels, Beers Criteria, FTC letters), so the epistemic score is low. Overall this is a somewhat better and more normalised world than 2028, with new bone and fracture costs.

Flaws are the hip-fracture arithmetic and the 5M long-term 65+ users (claim 2), 65+ users (~9.8M) equal to Medicare users (~9.8M), and a minor mismatch in how many states have bans.

least_plausible_claims.quote: CMS opens $149 Medicaid purchasing pool, 27 states join

least_plausible_claims.quote: The FDA-requested postmarketing study (2029, n≈61k) confirmed a clinically meaningful rise in ~6.5% of users versus ~2.8% of matched controls.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. A study requested in 2028 is reported in 2029 with a cohort nearly three times larger than the 2027 one. It also moves blunting from suspected to established, labelled and acted on by the FTC within about a year, which is implausibly fast.
